messages:
maria: Heads-up — we had a rate fanout incident this morning that looked like a sudden token double-count across ingress proxies. Prod client reports spiked 5x, admission immediately hit soft-shed and a chunk of traffic got dropped. Root timing ~06:12 UTC.
lee: :eyes: saw the alert. Any logs showing duplicate token IDs?
maria: Yes — the proxy trace shows the same client_token passed to two different edge pods within ~200ms. We currently shard counts by (token, pod) which let both pods increment.
jon: Oof. So the invariants assume single owner for token counts; fanout broke that. Was this caused by a retry or a route rebalancing?
maria: Early signal: upstream LB rebalanced active connections during a GC on one edge node. Client retried instantly with same token (replay), LB sent parallel requests to another pod.
andrew: We need to pick a path: make token counting centralized (single-writer) vs make local counters idempotent/deduped. Central looks simpler correctness-wise but adds latency.
lee: Agree. Tradeoffs we discussed earlier: central counter = single source of truth, consistent but higher p99; local with cross-pod dedupe = eventual, complicated reconciliation.
maria: For immediate mitigation I pushed a quick heuristic to the admission proxy: if token counts jump >200% within 1s across different pods, clamp to max(delta, 1) and emit a metric. That reduced drop rate.
jon: Can you paste the heuristic patch?
maria: Sure:
```
# ingress/admission/dedupe.py (hotfix)
def clamp_fanout(token, pod, observed_delta):
    if observed_delta > 0 and observed_delta > token.last_rate * 2:
        return min(observed_delta, int(token.last_rate * 2))
    return observed_delta
```
lee: Hotfix looks fine short-term. Need long-term design. My proposal: keep local fast-path but add a lightweight centralized lease for tokens that are above a threshold (heavy hitters). Lease grant time ~500ms, renewed if active. That keeps p99 for most, and centralizes costly tokens.
andrew: I like hybrid. Another option: enforce idempotency key on client side for retries — but can't rely on all clients. Also we could change sharding key to include a stable token_owner shard computed by consistent-hash(token) so requests usually go to the same pod. That reduces rebalancing risk.
maria: Consistent-hash is attractive but breaks during scaling events (migrations) unless we use virtual nodes. Also we still have cross-region LB cases.
jon: Thoughts on telemetry and debugability? We need a small trace id propagated and a fanout_score metric per token to trigger experiments.
lee: Add fanout_score to token telemetry (0..1) = fraction of parallel inflight per window. Alert if >0.3 for any token for >30s.
andrew: Proposed next steps: 1) Keep hotfix in place for 48h and monitor. 2) Run an experiment where ingress routes by consistent-hash (canary 5%). 3) Prototype centralized lease service (single-az) with 500–1000 qps target. 4) Add fanout_score metric and alerting.
maria: I'll own #1 and metrics. lee will own canary routing experiment. andrew + jon will pair on lease prototype.
jon: FYI I'll make a small RFC doc with latency SLO tradeoffs for central lease vs dedupe.
lee: Also add a runbook note: if soft-shed triggers, temporarily bump clamp multiplier to 3x and enable blocking of tokens with fanout_score>0.9.
maria: Thanks. File bug links here when you open them. deploy-bot: Deployed ingress hotfix to prod-edge group-3 at 06:25 UTC :white_check_mark:
